newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM to rebuff visiting Israeli minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM to rebuff visiting Israeli minister.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has spurned requests to meet Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy when he visits Turkey this week, Israel's ambassador in Ankara said on Monday.
Ambassador Zvi Elpeleg said Erbakan's office had ignored repeated requests for the meeting with Levy, who arrives on Tuesday for a two-day visit.

He said the reaction of the prime minister, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, flew in the face of assurances from top Erbakan aides that they would not undermine growing defence, commercial and political ties.
"I have received no response to my request three weeks ago to brief the prime minister on the Levy visit and no response on the (proposed) Levy meeting itself," Elpeleg told Reuters.
"No response is not included in the vocabulary of diplomatic protocol," he said. "We have it from different channels that (Erbakan) is trying to slip away from such a meeting."
Officials at the prime minister's office and the Foreign Ministry could not say if any meeting would take place.
Erbakan's Welfare Party won a slim plurality in general polls in 1995 after a campaign that included promises to renounce a military training pact with Israel.
Welfare alarmed Washington and its allies by demanding a general turn away from NATO-member Turkey's Western links in favour of expanded ties to Moslem countries.
Since taking power last summer, however, the party has softened many of its radical positions.
"Welfare cannot do without the support of Europe and the United States...but we are easy prey," Elpeleg said.
Levy's trip marks the first high-level visit since both countries formed new governments last summer.
A preliminary programme includes talks with Turkish President Suleyman Demirel, Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller and other ministers.
